purpose: Structured regimen-level sustainability metadata. Fields describe treatment-delivery footprint drivers and evidence readiness; they are not a carbon score or treatment recommendation.

status_values.catalogue_derived: Value obtained from existing SACTCheck catalogue metadata.
status_values.source_verified: Value verified against a current authoritative regimen/source.
status_values.locally_verified: Value verified against approved local operational/pharmacy data.
status_values.modelled: Value generated from an explicitly documented model and assumptions.
status_values.not_encoded: Relevant field has not yet been structured.
status_values.not_applicable: Field does not apply to this regimen.
status_values.evidence_required: A quantitative or comparative claim requires additional evidence before use.

route_classification.label: Route / delivery classification
route_classification.environmental_mechanism: Route influences infusion infrastructure, consumables, pharmacy handling, attendance and home-delivery opportunities.

administration_frequency.label: Administration frequency
administration_frequency.environmental_mechanism: Treatment frequency can affect travel, chair utilisation, pharmacy preparation and staff activity.

planned_treatment_encounters.label: Planned treatment encounters per cycle
planned_treatment_encounters.environmental_mechanism: More treatment encounters can increase facility and travel burden.

administration_time.label: Administration / chair time
administration_time.environmental_mechanism: Longer administration may increase facility, staffing and equipment utilisation.

ambulatory_pump.label: Ambulatory infusion pump
ambulatory_pump.environmental_mechanism: Pump use adds equipment and consumables and may create an additional connection/disconnection pathway.

cold_chain.label: Cold-chain requirement
cold_chain.environmental_mechanism: Temperature-controlled storage and transport can increase energy and logistics burden.

vial_presentation.label: Vial / presentation structure
vial_presentation.environmental_mechanism: Vial sizes and presentations influence residual medicine and packaging waste.

dose_banding.label: Dose-banding opportunity
dose_banding.environmental_mechanism: Where clinically and locally approved, dose banding can standardise preparation and potentially reduce waste.

vial_sharing.label: Vial-sharing opportunity
vial_sharing.environmental_mechanism: Where aseptic governance permits, vial sharing can reduce residual drug waste.

home_or_local_delivery.label: Home / local delivery potential
home_or_local_delivery.environmental_mechanism: Appropriate local or home pathways may reduce patient travel and central facility utilisation.

travel_model_inputs.label: Travel-model inputs
travel_model_inputs.environmental_mechanism: Travel emissions require patient- and service-level journey assumptions and are not inferred from regimen name alone.

Day 2: further fluorouracil bolus and a second 22-hour infusion; completion around Day 3. A repeating 14-day cycle. For adjuvant FOLFOX-4, NCCP describes 12 cycles; metastatic treatment continues while suitable.

administration_time.value: Two separate 22-hour fluorouracil infusions, starting Days 1 and 2; other infusions and review add time.

administration_time.value: Irinotecan infusion over 90 minutes; blood tests, review, premedication and observation add to the total visit.

administration_frequency.value: All four medicines are given by infusion on Day 1 of a 21-day cycle, for six cycles before surgery. Surgery findings guide the postoperative treatment. There is no routine take-home chemotherapy pump.

administration_time.value: Confirm blood tests, heart assessment, active medicines, route and the consent discussion. A cannula, PICC or implanted port may be used. If a port is chosen, a trained team inserts it in a separate procedure with local anaesthetic and sometimes sedation; the team explains fasting, blood-thinner and wound instructions. Trained staff check and access the line, give the prescribed premedicines and infusions, and monitor for reactions. Tell the nurse immediately about pain, burning, rash or breathlessness. This regimen does not routinely need a take-home infusion pump. Staff disconnect the infusion; a port is de-accessed when appropriate. Keep line-care and next-visit instructions. Full appointment duration and environmental effects have not been measured here.

administration_frequency.value: Four 21-day cycles: paclitaxel on Days 1, 8 and 15; carboplatin AUC 5 on Day 1. Pembrolizumab 200 mg on Day 1 of each cycle (every three weeks). Four further cycles (cycles 5–8): doxorubicin and cyclophosphamide on Day 1 every 21 days. Pembrolizumab 200 mg on Day 1 of each AC cycle. After surgery: pembrolizumab 200 mg every 21 days for nine doses OR 400 mg every 42 days for five doses. These are alternative schedules, not consecutive courses. Progression preventing definitive surgery or unacceptable pembrolizumab toxicity changes this plan; postoperative treatment is not automatic.

administration_time.value: IV infusions and AC administration as specified by the current phase. Complete visit duration, pharmacy time and observation are not quantified.

route_classification.source: NCCP 00619 v4a; checked 2026-10-17; https://healthservice.hse.ie/documents/6415/619_Abemaciclib.pdf Endocrine partner or ovarian suppression can add injection visits.

administration_frequency.value: Abemaciclib is taken twice daily continuously, with endocrine treatment, for up to two years if appropriate. A 28-day block is shown for orientation; there is no planned tablet-free week. Endocrine treatment usually continues longer.

administration_time.value: Oral medicines; blood, ECG and endocrine-injection visits depend on the selected plan.

planned_treatment_encounters.source: NCCP 00619 v4a; checked 2026-10-17; https://healthservice.hse.ie/documents/6415/619_Abemaciclib.pdf Visits for monitoring, surgery, radiation and endocrine treatment are not inferred from infusion count.

administration_frequency.value: Pertuzumab and trastuzumab are given by infusion every 21 days after the chemotherapy phase of the metastatic treatment plan. Duration depends on benefit, tolerance and the agreed plan; this is not a fixed one-year adjuvant course.

administration_time.value: Loading doses, premedication and observation change visit length. Use regimen-specific infusion times and local chair-time data.

planned_treatment_encounters.source: NCCP 00726 v3a; checked 2026-10-17; https://healthservice.hse.ie/documents/6599/726_v3a_Pertuzumab_trastuzumab.pdf Visits for monitoring, surgery, radiation and endocrine treatment are not inferred from infusion count.

administration_frequency.value: Ribociclib is taken once daily on Days 1–21, followed by seven days off, in a 28-day cycle. The endocrine partner continues according to its own prescription. Treatment continues while it is helping and tolerable.

administration_time.value: Oral medicines; blood, ECG and endocrine-injection visits depend on the selected plan.

planned_treatment_encounters.source: NCCP 00525 v6; checked 2026-10-17; https://healthservice.hse.ie/documents/6629/525_v6_Ribociclib_Metastatic_hghzyyD.pdf Visits for monitoring, surgery, radiation and endocrine treatment are not inferred from infusion count.

administration_frequency.value: Four AC treatments (doxorubicin 60 mg/m² and cyclophosphamide 600 mg/m²) 14 days apart, followed 14 days after the last AC by 12 weekly paclitaxel 80 mg/m² doses, subject to recovery. The planned sequence spans about 20 weeks.

administration_time.value: The unit confirms complete appointment duration; no environmental saving is measured here.

administration_frequency.value: Paclitaxel weekly for 12 doses with trastuzumab every 3 weeks; continue trastuzumab to complete one year of HER2 treatment when appropriate. The team selects IV trastuzumab or locally approved subcutaneous trastuzumab; these are alternative formulations, not additional medicines.

administration_time.value: The unit confirms full appointment duration; no environmental saving is measured here.

administration_frequency.value: T-DM1 by IV infusion every 21 days for 14 postoperative cycles, unless recurrence or unacceptable toxicity requires a change.

administration_time.value: Initial T-DM1 infusion 90 minutes plus 90-minute observation; later infusions 30 minutes plus 30-minute observation if tolerated.

administration_frequency.value: Ribociclib 400 mg once daily on Days 1–21, followed by Days 22–28 off, for up to 3 years. The aromatase inhibitor continues daily on its own schedule; ovarian suppression is added when indicated.

administration_time.value: Oral ribociclib; endocrine / ovarian-suppression and monitoring visits follow the selected plan.

administration_frequency.value: Tucatinib twice daily every day; capecitabine twice daily on Days 1–14 then off on Days 15–21; IV trastuzumab every 21 days. Continue while beneficial and tolerated, with clinician-approved changes.

administration_time.value: Oral tucatinib and capecitabine with IV trastuzumab every 3 weeks; infusion observation follows the protocol.

administration_frequency.value: IV trastuzumab every 21 days. Early breast cancer: complete one year total, allowing for earlier trastuzumab. Metastatic disease: continue while beneficial and tolerated; no automatic one-year stop.

administration_time.value: First infusion usually 90 minutes; later infusions may take 30 minutes if tolerated. NCCP observation is 6 hours from the start of the first infusion and 2 hours from the start of later infusions; ask about the unit’s approved policy.

administration_frequency.value: IV trastuzumab every 7 days, continuing while beneficial and tolerated. This weekly NCCP card is for metastatic disease, without a fixed one-year course.

administration_time.value: First infusion usually 90 minutes; later infusions may take 30 minutes if tolerated. NCCP observation is 6 hours from the start of the first infusion and 2 hours from the start of later infusions; ask about the unit’s approved policy.

administration_frequency.value: Trastuzumab 600 mg under the skin every 21 days, without a loading dose, while beneficial and tolerated. Any taxane or endocrine partner follows a separate prescription and monitoring plan.

administration_time.value: Injection over 2–5 minutes into alternate thighs. Observation is 30 minutes after the first injection and 15 minutes after subsequent injections, subject to approved local policy.

administration_frequency.value: Trastuzumab 600 mg under the skin every 21 days, without a loading dose, to complete one year total. Previous IV or combination-treatment trastuzumab counts towards that year; a route switch does not start a new year.

administration_time.value: Injection over 2–5 minutes into alternate thighs. Observation is 30 minutes after the first injection and 15 minutes after subsequent injections, subject to approved local policy.

administration_frequency.value: T-DM1 3.6 mg/kg IV every 21 days, adjusted if required, until progression or unacceptable toxicity. This metastatic course has no fixed 14-cycle endpoint; the postoperative early-breast regimen is a different card.

administration_time.value: First infusion over 90 minutes, then observe for at least 90 minutes. Later infusions may take 30 minutes if tolerated, with at least 30 minutes observation.

administration_frequency.value: Doxorubicin and cyclophosphamide on Day 1 every 21 days for four cycles. Any subsequent taxane follows a separately agreed regimen.

administration_time.value: Regimen-specific infusion and observation periods; full appointment time and environmental savings are not measured here.

administration_frequency.value: Four AC cycles 21 days apart, followed by 12 weekly paclitaxel doses. The team confirms recovery and the transition appointment.

administration_time.value: Regimen-specific infusion and observation periods; full appointment time and environmental savings are not measured here.

administration_frequency.value: Four AC cycles 14 days apart, followed by four paclitaxel doses 14 days apart. Growth-factor support accompanies the dose-dense course.

administration_time.value: Regimen-specific infusion and observation periods; full appointment time and environmental savings are not measured here.

administration_frequency.value: Four AC cycles every 14 days, then four fortnightly paclitaxel treatments with trastuzumab weekly on Days 1 and 8 of each 14-day block (eight weekly antibody doses). Trastuzumab then continues every 21 days to complete one year total; it is not given with AC.

administration_time.value: The unit confirms full appointment duration; no environmental saving is measured here.

administration_frequency.value: Four AC cycles 21 days apart, then 12 weekly paclitaxel doses with weekly trastuzumab. Continue trastuzumab to complete one year total, without overlapping it with AC.

administration_time.value: Regimen-specific infusion and observation periods; full appointment time and environmental savings are not measured here.

administration_frequency.value: Four AC cycles 14 days apart with growth-factor support, then 12 weekly paclitaxel doses with weekly trastuzumab. Continue trastuzumab to complete one year total; no concurrent AC / trastuzumab.

administration_time.value: The unit confirms full appointment duration; no environmental saving is measured here.

administration_frequency.value: Four AC cycles 14 days apart, followed by paclitaxel weekly for 12 doses and IV trastuzumab every 21 days. Trastuzumab then continues to complete one year total.

administration_time.value: The unit confirms full appointment duration; no environmental saving is measured here.

administration_frequency.value: Docetaxel 100 mg/m² by IV infusion on Day 1 every 21 days, with dose changes when needed. The number of cycles follows benefit, tolerance and the agreed treatment plan.

administration_time.value: The unit confirms complete appointment duration; no environmental saving is measured here.

administration_frequency.value: Docetaxel 75 mg/m² by IV infusion on Day 1 every 21 days. Duration depends on the cancer and treatment aim: NSCLC has a source maximum of six cycles; other indications require an explicitly agreed course, including prostate treatment. This differs from the 100 mg/m² card.

administration_time.value: Infusion and observation times differ by drug and first versus later doses; the unit confirms the full visit duration, including blood review and preparation.

administration_frequency.value: Docetaxel and cyclophosphamide on Day 1 every 21 days for four to six cycles. The team confirms the planned course before treatment. Radiotherapy, when indicated, follows chemotherapy.

administration_time.value: Regimen-specific infusion and observation periods; full appointment time and environmental savings are not measured here.

administration_frequency.value: Paclitaxel and IV trastuzumab weekly for 12 weeks, then trastuzumab alone to complete one year total. Continuation can be weekly or every 3 weeks under the source-specific plan; the treatment aim remains adjuvant.

administration_time.value: The unit confirms full appointment duration; no environmental saving is measured here.

administration_frequency.value: Paclitaxel 80 mg/m² on Days 1, 8 and 15 of each 28-day cycle. Day 22 is a planned week off, not a fourth routine dose. Continue according to benefit and tolerance. The NCCP indications are off-label in Ireland and require the local consent / approval process.

administration_time.value: Infusion and observation times differ by drug and first versus later doses; the unit confirms the full visit duration, including blood review and preparation.

administration_frequency.value: Default: six 21-day TCH cycles with IV trastuzumab, then trastuzumab alone to complete one year total. The source also permits weekly IV or fixed-dose SC trastuzumab alternatives; the team confirms the formulation and visit schedule.

administration_frequency.value: Six 21-day cycles before surgery: IV pertuzumab, fixed-dose trastuzumab under the skin, IV docetaxel and IV carboplatin. Surgery and pathology guide the postoperative HER2 plan. This is not the combined Phesgo injection.

administration_time.value: Confirm blood tests, heart assessment, active medicines, route and the consent discussion. A cannula, PICC or implanted port may be used. If a port is chosen, a trained team inserts it in a separate procedure with local anaesthetic and sometimes sedation; the team explains fasting, blood-thinner and wound instructions. IV pertuzumab and chemotherapy still require venous access. Trastuzumab 600 mg is a separate thigh injection; this is not Phesgo. Staff check the line, give prescribed premedicines and treatment, and observe for reactions. Tell them immediately about burning, pain, rash or breathlessness. This regimen does not routinely need a take-home infusion pump. Staff disconnect the infusion; a port is de-accessed when appropriate. Keep line-care and next-visit instructions. Full appointment duration and environmental effects have not been measured here.

administration_frequency.value: IV pertuzumab, IV trastuzumab and docetaxel every 21 days. Docetaxel duration is reviewed separately; the two HER2 antibodies may continue after chemotherapy stops while beneficial and tolerated.

administration_time.value: Confirm blood tests, heart assessment, active medicines, route and the consent discussion. A cannula, PICC or implanted port may be used. administration_frequency.value: Paclitaxel on Days 1, 8 and 15 of each 21-day block, for up to eight cycles; IV pertuzumab and trastuzumab on Day 1. This NCCP alternative applies when docetaxel is unsuitable, not tolerated or caused significant toxicity. Antibodies may continue after the taxane stops while beneficial and tolerated.

administration_time.value: Confirm blood tests, heart assessment, active medicines, route and the consent discussion. A cannula, PICC or implanted port may be used. If a port is chosen, a trained team inserts it in a separate procedure with local anaesthetic and sometimes sedation; the team explains fasting, blood-thinner and wound instructions. Staff check the line, give prescribed premedicines and treatment, and observe for reactions. Tell them immediately about burning, pain, rash or breathlessness. administration_frequency.value: Eribulin on Days 1 and 8 of each 21-day cycle. Day 15 is a planned treatment-free week. Treatment continues while beneficial and tolerated.

administration_time.value: Eribulin is given by IV infusion over 5 minutes; blood review, preparation and access make the full visit longer.

administration_frequency.value: Eribulin on Days 1 and 15 of each 28-day cycle. Days 8 and 22 are planned treatment-free weeks. This alternative schedule requires a specific discussion and consent.

administration_time.value: The unit confirms complete appointment duration; no environmental saving is measured here.

administration_frequency.value: Nab-paclitaxel on Day 1 every 21 days. Review response after two cycles; the NCCP protocol says to discontinue if there is no response. Further treatment depends on benefit and tolerance.

administration_time.value: The unit confirms complete appointment duration; no environmental saving is measured here.

administration_frequency.value: Nab-paclitaxel on Days 1, 8 and 15 of each 28-day cycle, with a planned week off on Day 22. Continue while beneficial and tolerated. This off-label schedule requires specific consent.

administration_time.value: The unit confirms complete appointment duration; no environmental saving is measured here.

administration_frequency.value: Pegylated liposomal doxorubicin on Day 1 every 28 days, typically for six cycles or until progression or unacceptable toxicity. The team confirms the intended duration and reviews benefit.

administration_time.value: The first infusion starts at 1 mg per minute. Later infusions may take 60 minutes if there was no reaction; a previous reaction requires a modified supervised schedule.

administration_frequency.value: Take tamoxifen once daily continuously. There is no planned week off. The prescriber confirms the duration for the treatment setting.

administration_time.value: Swallow the tablet whole, with or without food. If a dose is missed or vomited, do not replace it; take the next scheduled daily dose.

administration_frequency.value: Take anastrozole once daily continuously. There is no planned week off. The treatment setting determines the intended duration.

administration_time.value: Swallow with water, with or without food. Do not replace a missed or vomited dose; resume the next scheduled dose.

administration_frequency.value: Take letrozole once daily continuously. The prescriber confirms whether the aim is before surgery, after surgery, extended adjuvant treatment or advanced-disease control.

administration_time.value: Take with or without food. Take a forgotten dose when remembered unless the next dose is within about two to three hours; then skip it. Do not take two doses together.

administration_frequency.value: Take exemestane once daily continuously, preferably after a meal. There is no planned week off. Confirm the prior-treatment and duration plan.

administration_time.value: Take the tablet after a meal. Skip a missed dose and continue at the next scheduled time; do not double the dose.

administration_frequency.value: NCCP schedule: 500 mg on Days 1 and 15 of the first 28-day cycle, then Day 1 of each 28-day cycle. This means Day 29 next, then every 28 days.

administration_time.value: Each usual 500 mg dose is given as two 5 mL injections, one in each buttock, slowly over one to two minutes per injection. This is not an intravenous infusion; no port or pump is needed for fulvestrant itself.

route_classification.note: Palbociclib is oral; an aromatase-inhibitor partner is oral, while fulvestrant or ovarian-suppression injections add parenteral visits. Use the actual prescribed partner for travel and resource estimates.

administration_frequency.value: Take palbociclib for 21 days, then have 7 days without palbociclib. The aromatase-inhibitor tablet continues every day, or fulvestrant injections follow their separate schedule. The week off applies to palbociclib, not automatically to the hormone treatment.

administration_time.value: Check whether the pharmacy supplied capsules or tablets: capsules are taken with food; tablets can be taken with or without food. Swallow whole at a consistent time. Avoid grapefruit. If you miss or vomit a dose, do not take an extra dose; take the next scheduled dose. Do not restart after a clinical hold until the treating team confirms.

administration_frequency.value: Both tablets are taken every day continuously. There is no planned week off. A four-week blood-test review is a monitoring interval, not a stop-and-restart treatment cycle.

administration_time.value: Take everolimus at the same time daily, consistently with food or consistently without food. Take exemestane after a meal. Swallow tablets whole with water; do not crush or chew. If a dose is missed, take the next scheduled dose without adding an extra dose.

administration_frequency.value: One infusion on Day 1 of a 21-day cycle. The next infusion is normally three weeks later. A delayed appointment is rescheduled by the team; patients do not calculate catch-up doses.

administration_time.value: The first infusion takes 90 minutes. Later infusions may take 30 minutes if the previous infusion was tolerated. Allow extra time for assessment, anti-sickness medicines and any observation. A cannula or an existing central line can be used according to the clinical plan; there is no home pump.

administration_frequency.value: Two treatment visits in each three-week cycle: Day 1, then Day 8. There is no planned infusion on Day 15. The next cycle starts after Day 21 if the team confirms it is appropriate.

administration_time.value: The first infusion takes about three hours; later infusions usually take one to two hours if the earlier infusion was tolerated. Premedicines, checks and at least 30 minutes of observation after every infusion add to the visit. No take-home infusion pump is part of this regimen.

administration_frequency.value: Take olaparib tablets morning and evening every day. There is no planned week off. Blood-review appointments are usually every four weeks during this one-year breast course.

administration_time.value: Swallow tablets whole with water, with or without food. Do not chew, crush, dissolve or divide them. If a dose is missed, take the next normal dose at its usual time; do not double it. Check tablet strength after any dose change.

administration_frequency.value: Phesgo on Day 1 every 21 days after the chemotherapy component is complete; continue while beneficial and tolerated. This is active metastatic maintenance, not a fixed one-year adjuvant course.

administration_time.value: Loading/reloading 1200 mg/600 mg over 8 minutes with 30 minutes observation; maintenance 600 mg/600 mg over 5 minutes with 15 minutes observation. Alternate thighs; avoid sore, bruised or damaged skin. Full visit time is not measured here.

administration_frequency.value: Phesgo and docetaxel on Day 1 every 21 days. Docetaxel is planned for at least six cycles; it may stop after 6–8 cycles or toxicity. Phesgo may continue alone while beneficial and tolerated.

administration_time.value: Loading/reloading 1200 mg/600 mg over 8 minutes with 30 minutes observation; maintenance 600 mg/600 mg over 5 minutes with 15 minutes observation. Complete the observation before chemotherapy. Alternate thighs; avoid sore, bruised or damaged skin. Full visit time is not measured here.

administration_frequency.value: Phesgo on Day 1 and paclitaxel on Days 1, 8 and 15 of a 21-day cycle, for up to eight paclitaxel cycles. Phesgo may continue alone while beneficial and tolerated.

administration_time.value: Loading/reloading 1200 mg/600 mg over 8 minutes with 30 minutes observation; maintenance 600 mg/600 mg over 5 minutes with 15 minutes observation. Complete the observation before chemotherapy. Alternate thighs; avoid sore, bruised or damaged skin. Full visit time is not measured here.

administration_frequency.value: Six 21-day cycles before surgery: Phesgo, docetaxel and carboplatin on Day 1. Surgery and pathology determine the postoperative HER2 medicine and remaining course.

administration_time.value: Loading/reloading 1200 mg/600 mg over 8 minutes with 30 minutes observation; maintenance 600 mg/600 mg over 5 minutes with 15 minutes observation. Complete the observation before chemotherapy. Alternate thighs; avoid sore, bruised or damaged skin. Full visit time is not measured here.

administration_frequency.value: Four 21-day cycles: paclitaxel on Days 1, 8 and 15; carboplatin AUC 1.5 on Days 1, 8 and 15. Pembrolizumab 200 mg on Day 1 of each cycle (every three weeks). After surgery: pembrolizumab 200 mg every 21 days for nine doses OR 400 mg every 42 days for five doses. These are alternative schedules, not consecutive courses. Progression preventing definitive surgery or unacceptable pembrolizumab toxicity changes this plan; postoperative treatment is not automatic.

administration_frequency.value: Lapatinib once daily on Days 1–21, continuously. Capecitabine twice daily on Days 1–14, then no capecitabine on Days 15–21. Repeat every 21 days while beneficial and tolerated. The capecitabine rest week is not a lapatinib rest week.

administration_time.value: Confirm DPD result, blood tests, cardiac assessment, medicines review and the two tablet schedules. Confirm tablet strengths, doses, Days 1–14 for capecitabine and continuous lapatinib. Keep in the original packaging and out of reach of children. Take lapatinib at least one hour before or after food, consistently in the same relation to meals. Take capecitabine with food or within 30 minutes after eating. Swallow tablets whole. A pharmacist can help arrange the different food timings. Keep blood and clinical-review appointments even though treatment is at home. Bring your medicine list and tell the team about missed or held doses. Full appointment duration and environmental effects have not been measured here.

administration_frequency.value: IV pertuzumab and IV trastuzumab every 21 days. Before surgery: 3–6 cycles alongside the selected chemotherapy. After surgery: up to 18 cycles overall under the agreed adjuvant plan. If an anthracycline is used first, finish it before starting these antibodies with the taxane phase. Confirm the exact companion regimen and local access.

administration_time.value: Confirm the active regimen, blood results, cardiac checks, medicines review, route and consent discussion. A cannula, PICC or implanted port may be used. If a port is chosen, a trained team inserts it in a separate procedure with local anaesthetic and sometimes sedation; the team explains fasting, blood-thinner and wound instructions. Staff check the line, give prescribed premedicines and treatment, and observe for reactions. Tell them immediately about burning, pain, rash or breathlessness. This regimen does not routinely need a take-home infusion pump. Staff disconnect the infusion; a port is de-accessed when appropriate. Keep line-care and next-visit instructions. Full appointment duration and environmental effects have not been measured here.

administration_time.value: Confirm blood results, cardiac checks, active phase, previous dual HER2 dose and the consent discussion. Loading/reloading 1200 mg/600 mg over 8 minutes with 30 minutes observation; maintenance 600 mg/600 mg over 5 minutes with 15 minutes observation. Complete the observation before chemotherapy. Alternate thighs; avoid sore, bruised or damaged skin. After Phesgo observation, receive the prescribed IV vinorelbine or follow the separately agreed oral dose plan. Phesgo itself needs no IV line; the oral vinorelbine option also avoids an infusion. IV vinorelbine still needs a cannula, PICC or port. No take-home infusion pump is routinely used. Confirm supportive medicines, next visits and due tests. Injection time is shorter than the whole appointment; preparation, assessment and observation still take time. Full appointment duration and environmental effects have not been measured here.
